claim: Ausbruch sits between Beerenauslese and Trockenbeerenauslese on the Austrian must-weight ladder, and its name comes from breaking the shrivelled berries out of the bunch.
because: That was the old Pradikat (27 KMW). Under the current Weingesetz 2009, §11, Ausbruch is no longer a separate step. A Trockenbeerenauslese (minimum 30 KMW) from the Freistadt Rust may be labelled 'Ruster Ausbruch', and the name may only be used together with 'Rust'. This restriction has applied since 2016. The Ruster Ausbruch DAC Verordnung also sets a minimum must weight of 30 KMW, from botrytised berries shrivelled naturally on the vine and picked by selective hand harvest.
fix: Ausbruch once sat between Beerenauslese and Trockenbeerenauslese on the Austrian must-weight ladder; today the name belongs to Rust alone and requires Trockenbeerenauslese must weight (30 KMW). The name comes from breaking the shrivelled berries out of the bunch.
